post.description:
The body names exactly one source:
- `file_name` plus `file_data_base64` uploads a `.crx`/`.zip`.
- `source_path` reads a `.crx`/`.zip`, or packs an unpacked extension
  directory, from the machine running Donut. `link: true` loads that
  directory in place instead, so edits apply on the next browser start;
  a linked extension is machine-local and never syncs.

`name` may be omitted: the manifest's own name is preferred anyway, and it
is only an error when the manifest has none either.

400.description: No source, two sources, undecodable payload, unsupported file type, or an unreadable unpacked directory

put.summary: Replace an extension's payload, rename it, or both.
put.description:
Sources are the same as on create, and every field is optional — but a body
carrying neither a name nor a source asks for nothing and is refused rather
than answered with an unchanged extension.

400.description: Nothing to change, two sources, undecodable payload, unsupported file type, or an unreadable unpacked directory

404.description: Extension not found, or source_path does not exist

400.description: Bad request
Bad request

post.description:
- `browser` must be `"wayfern"`; any other value is rejected
  with 400.
- `version` is optional: omit it or pass `"latest"` to use the newest
  already-downloaded version of that browser. The version must be present
  locally (this endpoint does not download new versions); 400 if none is.
- Omitting the matching `wayfern_config`, or passing an
  empty object `{}`, generates a fresh fingerprint automatically.
- `wayfern_config.os` picks the fingerprint OS (`"windows"`, `"macos"`,
  `"linux"`, `"android"`, `"ios"`). Omit it to match the host. Any other
  OS is cross-OS spoofing and needs an active Pro plan; 402 otherwise.
  A `wayfern_config` that fails to parse is a 400, never a silent default.
- Pro accounts may generate 100 profiles per rolling hour; the 101st is
  refused with 429 and a `retryAfterSeconds` in the body.

navigated.description: Whether a page load followed the click.

click_count.description: 1 (default), 2 for a double click, 3 for a triple.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the click. Default 60000, ceiling 300000.

candidate_limit.description: How many candidates an ambiguity error lists. Default 10, ceiling 100.

clear_first.description: Empty the field first. Default true.

typos.description: Mistype and correct a few characters, as a hand does. Default true.

wpm.description:
Target words per minute. Honoured by the fallback engine only: Wayfern
152 types at the profile's own rhythm.

corrections.description:
Mistyped characters that were corrected. Absent on the fallback engine,
which does not count its own.

cloud_sync_enabled.description: Convenience form of `sync_mode` — true for Regular or Encrypted.

ephemeral.description: Browsing data is kept in memory only.

extension_group_id.description:
Extension group loaded into the browser at launch. Settable via
`PUT /v1/profiles/{id}`; exposed here so a caller can read back what it
set instead of having to go through the desktop app.

fingerprint_os.description:
The fingerprint operating system set at creation via `wayfern_config.os`
(`"windows"`, `"macos"`, `"linux"`, `"android"` or `"ios"`), or `null`
when the fingerprint was generated for the host. This is what the browser
reports to sites; `host_os` is the machine the profile was created on and
is a different thing.

host_os.description:
OS the profile was created on (`"macos"`, `"windows"`, `"linux"`).
`null` when neither `host_os` nor the browser config records one.

is_cross_os.description:
True when the profile belongs to a different OS than this machine.
Such a profile cannot be launched locally, and must only ever run on a
remote host of its own OS — Chromium profile state is OS-specific.

remote_debugging_port.description: CDP remote-debugging port when the profile is currently running locally. `null` when stopped, so API clients can drive the browser over CDP without a separate `/run` round-trip.

sync_mode.description:
Cloud sync mode: `"Disabled"`, `"Regular"` or `"Encrypted"`.
Settable via `PUT /v1/profiles/{id}`; exposed here so a caller can read
back what it set, and so a remote-launch caller can tell whether the
profile is actually available in cloud storage.

temporary.description: Created for one automation run: deleted when its browser stops.

ApiRemoteSessionsResponse.description:
Every remote session the signed-in account currently owns.

`run-remote` hands back a session id and the literal string `provisioning`;
without a way to read the real state back, an automation client can only
discover that a session became usable by trying to drive it.

url.description: Optional URL to open in every launched profile.

error.description: Failure reason if not launched, otherwise null.

remote_debugging_port.description: Remote debugging port if launched, otherwise null.

error.description: Failure reason if not stopped, otherwise null.

ok.description: Whether this profile was stopped successfully.

CookieBotConflict.description: A teammate's enrolment of the same profile.

overlaps.description:
Set on the dry-run check: the two enrolments share a weekday and fire
within an hour of each other.

CookieBotLimits.description:
The bounds the schedule routes actually enforce, as this build reads them.

Every field is optional because a server that predates `limits` sends none
of them, and a client that read a missing bound as `0` would refuse every
value the form can produce. Only the bounds the desktop acts on are decoded
— serde drops the rest, and this struct is what the GUI ultimately receives,
so adding a field here is what makes one reachable from TypeScript.

max_slots.description: Most entries a calendar may carry.

max_template_name_length.description: Longest name a saved site list may be given.

CookieBotPreset.description:
A named intensity the user can pick. The client never learns what it
expands to; only enough to label the choice and show its rough cost.

name.description:
Server-supplied English label, present only so a preset added after this
build still renders. The UI must prefer its own `t()` key for a known id.

default_preset.description:
Which preset the server suggests when the user has expressed no
preference.

oneOf.description:
The server's own bounds, when it publishes them. The desktop mirrors a
copy for offline form validation; these win where they disagree.

templates.description:
The curated templates on offer. Served beside the presets so a template
added server-side appears without a desktop release.

CookieBotRun.description: One night's work on one profile.

chunks_total.description:
How many browser sessions this night is split into, and which one is
running. "chunk 2 of 3" is the only honest way to report a night the
server split.

dispatch_after.description: The jittered instant the run was allowed to start.

max_minutes.description: The night's whole budget, which may be split across several chunks.

outcome_code.description: Why it ended the way it did, e.g. `profile_locked`, `no_capacity`.

next_before.description: Keyset cursor; `None` on the last page.

CookieBotSchedule.description: A profile enrolled in the nightly bot.

blocked_by.description:
Why tonight would be refused, or `None`.

The server computes this on every read precisely so a broken enrolment is
visible the moment it breaks. Dropping it meant a profile whose proxy was
detached in the afternoon still showed a healthy row and a next-run time,
and first announced itself with a skipped run at 02:00.

days_mask.description: The first slot's weekdays, bit 0 = Monday. See `run_at_minute`.

preset.description: Server-issued preset id. Opaque here — what it expands to is the server's.

profile_state_at.description: When those facts were last refreshed.

proxy_remote_reachable.description:
Whether that exit is one a remote host could dial. Defaults to false on an
older server that does not send it, which reads as "not reachable" and is
the safe direction.

run_at_minute.description:
Minutes past local midnight the FIRST slot is anchored to. The server
mirrors `slots[0]` onto this pair on every write.

slots.description:
Every time-of-day this enrolment fires.

`default` rather than required because a server older than multi-slot
scheduling sends only the mirrored pair above, and a decode failure there
would blank the whole Cookie Bot surface rather than show one time instead
of several. Callers must therefore fall back to the pair when this is
empty — never treat an empty list as "fires at no time".

template_id.description:
The template the sites came from, or `None` for the user's own list.

A built-in id (`low-intent-purchaser`) means `sites` is EMPTY on purpose:
its URLs are server-owned and never sent to a client. A `user:<uuid>` id
is provenance only — those sites were copied onto the enrolment and are
present below.

conflicts.description:
Repeated on a successful acknowledged write so the UI can keep showing
the warning rather than pretending the collision went away.

CookieBotSlot.description:
One time-of-day an enrolment fires, on a set of local weekdays.

Copy, and deliberately tiny: a calendar is a list of these, and the desktop
rebuilds that list on every keystroke in the enrolment form.

days_mask.description: Bitmask of local weekdays, bit 0 = Monday. At least one bit set.

run_at_minute.description: Minutes past local midnight, in the schedule's timezone.

CookieBotTemplate.description:
A server-owned browsing template: a named answer to "what is this profile
for", which the user picks INSTEAD of typing a site list.

Carries no URLs, and must not gain any: the site pool a template draws from
is server-owned, and a published list is one a retailer can filter.

name.description:
Server-supplied English label and blurb, present only so a template added
after this build still renders. The UI prefers its own `t()` key for an id
it recognises.

site_count.description: How many sites this template browses. Not which.

CookieBotUsage.description: The team owner's after-the-fact view of who spent what.

runs_failed.description:
How many of those runs did not do what they were asked. Its sibling on the
member view is `bot_runs_failed`; both are on the wire and both belong in
the report.

CreateExtensionRequest.description:
Add an extension from exactly one source: an uploaded payload
(`file_name` together with `file_data_base64`), or `source_path` on the
machine running Donut. Supplying both, or neither, is a 400.

file_data_base64.description: Payload bytes, standard base64. Only meaningful with `file_name`.

file_name.description: Name of the uploaded file. Its suffix picks the type: `.crx` or `.zip`.

link.description:
Load a `source_path` directory in place instead of copying it into the
store, so edits to the folder apply on the next browser start. Directory
sources only, and a linked extension never syncs.

name.description:
Display name. Optional — the manifest's own name wins when it has one,
and a blank name is only rejected when the manifest has none either.

source_path.description:
Path on this machine: a `.crx`/`.zip`, or an unpacked extension
directory holding a top-level `manifest.json`.

browser.description:
Browser engine. Must be `"wayfern"` (anti-detect Chromium). Any other
value (e.g. `"chromium"`) is rejected with 400.

ephemeral.description:
Keep the profile's browsing data in memory only, so nothing it browses
reaches real disk. Defaults to false.

proxy_id.description:
Optional stored-proxy id. Omit it, send `null`, or send an empty string
for a profile with no proxy. Mutually exclusive with `vpn_id`.

temporary.description:
A profile for one automation run: implies `ephemeral`, is destroyed when
its browser stops, and is swept at startup if it outlived a crash.
Defaults to false.

version.description:
Optional. Omit (or pass `"latest"`) to use the newest already-downloaded
version of the chosen browser. A concrete version must already be
downloaded; the create path does not fetch new versions.

vpn_id.description:
Optional stored-VPN id. Omit it, send `null`, or send an empty string for
a profile with no VPN. Mutually exclusive with `proxy_id`.

wayfern_config.description:
Wayfern fingerprint/config. Send only when `browser` is `"wayfern"`.
Omit it, or pass an empty object `{}`, to have a fresh fingerprint
generated automatically at creation. Provide a `fingerprint` field to
pin a specific one.

pairs.description: Profile/proxy pairs to apply, one proxy per profile.

Engine.description: Which implementation answered a tool call.

linked_path.description:
Absolute directory this extension is loaded from in place. `Some` means
nothing is copied into the store: Chromium reads the folder directly, so
edits land on the next browser start. Linked extensions are machine-local
and never sync.

manifest_name.description: The archive's identity, kept separately from the user's editable name.

source_kind.description:
`archive` or `unpacked`. Absent in metadata written before unpacked
support, which is exactly the archive case.

Extraction.description: The rows an extraction produced and why it stopped.

byteSize.description: Byte length of the compact JSON serialization of `rows`.

ExtractionField.description: One output column of a structured extraction.

key.description: The key this column appears under in each row's values.

locator.description: Evaluated inside each container; the first match wins.

container.description: Matches every row container; several matches are the expected case.

field_map.description: The columns. The browser calls this `fieldMap`; `fields` is accepted too.

max_nodes.description: Node cap for each snapshot. Default 20000, ceiling 200000.

oneOf.description: The control clicked to advance a page. Absent means one page.

ExtractionRow.description: One extracted row. A field that matched nothing is an absent key.

page.description: Zero-based page this row came from.

content.description:
Raw cookie file content. Format is auto-detected: a JSON array
(Puppeteer / EditThisCookie style) or a Netscape `cookies.txt`.

allow_running.description:
Import even though the source browser is running. Databases are still
snapshotted consistently, but LevelDB site data may be mid-write.

browser_type.description:
The source browser family (`chromium`, `brave`, `edge`, …). Load-bearing:
it selects which Keychain / secret-service item holds the key that
unlocks the source's cookies and passwords.

oneOf.description:
How to handle an already-taken profile name: "skip" or "rename"
(auto-suffix). Defaults to "rename".

group_id.description: Optional group to assign every imported profile to.

items.description: Profiles to import. Each item is isolated — one failure doesn't stop the rest.

wayfern_config.description:
Wayfern fingerprint/config applied to every imported profile. Omit to
have fresh fingerprints generated automatically.

format.description:
"txt" — one proxy per line (`host:port`, `host:port:user:pass`, or URL
forms like `http://user:pass@host:port`). "json" — a Donut proxy export.

name_prefix.description: Name prefix for txt imports; proxies are named "{prefix} Proxy {n}".

name.description: Optional display name; defaults to filename-based name

LocatorAttribute.description: One `name=value` pair a locator requires, or a matched node carries.

LocatorBounds.description: Where a matched node is, in root-document CSS pixels.

LocatorCandidate.description:
Everything a caller needs about one matched node.

`value` is omitted, never blanked, for a control the page marked protected;
`backendNodeId` is absent only on the fallback engine, which has no DOM
agent behind it.

signature.description: Per-profile deterministic identifier for the node's structural position.

LocatorDescription.description:
How a caller names an element without a selector.

Mirrors the locator shape the browser takes. Keys are the browser's own
(`nameContains`, `textContains`); the snake_case spellings are accepted on
input so a REST body written in this API's usual style still parses.

attributes.description: Attribute pairs that must all match.

name.description: Computed accessible name, exact after whitespace collapse.

role.description: AX role token, matched case- and separator-insensitively.

text.description: Visible text content, from the live layout.

LocatorResolution.description: A locator resolved to exactly one node.

locator.description: The canonical form of the locator that resolved.

matchCount.description: Always 1: present so a caller can assert it rather than infer it.

PerceptionFrame.description: One frame of a perception snapshot.

PerceptionNode.description: One node of a perception snapshot.

checked.description: "true", "false" or "mixed"; absent for anything not checkable.

x.description: Root-document page coordinates in CSS pixels, unclipped.

PerceptionPage.description:
A perception snapshot, or as much of one as the byte cap allowed.

When `truncated` is true a `cursor` follows: pass it back to continue from
where this call stopped.

text.description: Readable text for exactly the nodes returned.

PerceptionRequest.description:
What a caller may ask `Wayfern.capturePagePerception` for.

Field names are this API's snake_case; the browser's camelCase spellings
are accepted too.

budget_ms.description: Capture budget in milliseconds. Default 5000, clamped to [100, 60000].

cursor.description: Continue an earlier capture from the cursor it returned.

max_bytes.description: Total byte cap across cursor pages. Default 1 MiB, ceiling 4 MiB.

max_nodes.description: Per-frame node ceiling. Default 100000; 0 for no limit.

viewport_only.description: Drop nodes outside the viewport. Default false.

PerceptionStats.description: How much a capture covered, and how much it cost.

bytes.description: Serialized size of the nodes and text returned.

framesFailed.description: Frames whose renderer did not answer within the budget.

totalNodes.description: Nodes in the whole snapshot, not on this page.

PickedElement.description: What the user clicked while the picker was armed.

locator.description: The smallest description that still resolves to this node.

matchCount.description:
How many nodes `locator` matches; more than 1 when the page genuinely
holds indistinguishable elements.

error.description: Structured `{"code": …}` error string when status is "failed".

oneOf.description: What actually came across. Present when status is "imported".

ProfileImportReport.description: Per-profile outcome, returned alongside each item in a batch import.

cookies_migrated.description: Cookies whose value is readable in the new profile.

cookies_unrecoverable.description: Cookies carried over as rows but whose value could not be recovered.

passwords_migrated.description: Saved logins whose secret is readable in the new profile. `passwords_migrated` on the wire.

passwords_unrecoverable.description: Saved logins carried as rows whose secret could not be recovered. `passwords_unrecoverable` on the wire.

payment_methods_migrated.description: Saved cards / IBANs / autofill secrets re-encrypted.

warnings.description: Stable codes from [`warning`], deduplicated, in insertion order.

ProxyAssignmentResult.description: What happened to one profile in an apply.

error.description: A `{"code": ...}` payload when `ok` is false, otherwise null.

ProxyPair.description: One profile and the proxy it should end up on.

RemoteHoursQuota.description:
The remote-hour budget as the server reports it, with the bot/interactive
breakdown it sends.

members.description: The full roster for an owner or admin; just the caller otherwise.

RemoteSessionState.description:
A session as the backend currently sees it.

`POST /api/remote-sessions` hands back the literal string `provisioning`
and nothing else, so until this type existed the only way to observe a
session becoming usable was to keep trying to drive it.

billed_seconds.description:
What it has cost so far. A live session is already being charged, so this
is the running wall clock rather than 0 until it closes.

cdp_ready.description: The relay is up, so the session can actually be driven.

close_reason.description: Why it ended: `stopped_by_user`, `max_duration`, `lost the profile lock`…

ended_at.description:
When it finished. The backend sends one timestamp, not a
`ready_at`/`closed_at` pair.

run_id.description: Set when this session belongs to a cookie-bot run.

state.description:
`provisioning` | `ready` | `live` | `closed` | `error`.

Named `state` because that is what the cloud API actually sends. It
carried the name `status` until a real payload was compared against it,
and because the field had no
default, every list and single read failed at `missing field \`status\``
and surfaced as CLOUD_UNREACHABLE. The alias keeps the launch reply —
which predates the reconciled vocabulary and still says `status` —
decoding through the same type.

team_id.description: The team the hours are attributed to, when the caller belongs to one.

url.description: Optional URL to open once the remote browser is up.

platform.description: Operating system the session was scheduled onto — always the profile's own.

session_id.description: Remote session id, for polling or closing the session.

mode.description:
`Disabled`, `Regular`, or `Encrypted`.

`Encrypted` derives its key from a passphrase that never leaves this
machine, so a profile in that mode can be synced but NOT run remotely —
a remote host would download ciphertext it cannot decrypt.

remote_launchable.description: Whether the profile can now be launched on a remote host.

SetCookieBotScheduleRequest.description:
Enrol a profile in the nightly cookie bot, or replace its enrolment.

`platform` and `profile_name` are optional because this machine already
knows both: the platform is the profile's own operating system, and a
caller-supplied one that disagrees is a mistake, not a choice.

acknowledge_conflict.description:
Write anyway when a teammate already enrols this profile. Without it, a
colliding write is refused with 409 and the teammate's details.

days_mask.description: Bitmask of local weekdays, bit 0 = Monday (1..127).

enabled.description: Whether the nightly run is armed. A disabled schedule keeps its settings.

jitter_seconds.description: Random spread around the anchor time, in seconds.

max_minutes.description: Upper bound on one run, in minutes.

platform.description:
`windows`, `macos` or `linux`. Defaults to the profile's own operating
system, and must match it when supplied.

profile_name.description: Defaults to the profile's local name.

run_at_minute.description: Minutes past local midnight the run is anchored to (0..1439).

sites.description: Absolute http(s) URLs to browse. The bot visits only these.

timezone.description: IANA zone the run time is expressed in.

max_minutes.description: Overrides the schedule's own cap for this run only.

profile_id.description:
Profile to warm. It must already have a schedule: the preset and the site
list live there, so a run never carries a behaviour of its own.

billed_seconds.description: What the session actually cost, in seconds.

extension_ids.description:
Replaces the whole membership list. Omit to leave it untouched; use the
`/extensions/{extension_id}` sub-routes to add or remove one member.

UpdateExtensionRequest.description:
Replace an extension's payload, rename it, or both. Every field is
optional, but a request that carries neither a name nor a source has
nothing to do and is a 400.

file_data_base64.description: Replacement payload bytes, standard base64. Only meaningful with `file_name`.

file_name.description: Name of the replacement upload. Its suffix picks the type: `.crx` or `.zip`.

link.description: Load a `source_path` directory in place instead of copying it in.

source_path.description:
Path on this machine to re-import from: a `.crx`/`.zip`, or an unpacked
extension directory.

clear_on_close.description:
Wipe browsing data (keeping extensions and bookmarks) when the browser
exits. Rejected (400) for ephemeral or password-protected profiles.

proxy_id.description:
Omitted or `null` leaves the proxy assignment unchanged; an empty string
detaches it. Assigning a proxy clears any assigned VPN.

vpn_id.description:
Omitted or `null` leaves the VPN assignment unchanged; an empty string
detaches it. Assigning a VPN clears any assigned proxy.
